title: Olen käyttänyt tätä huoltamoa monta vuotta
subtitle: I have used this repair shop for many years

blocks.text: Every past tense so far — oli, sain, tehtiin — describes one finished action. But long-time customers in this corpus reach for a different shape when they want to say 'I have used this place for years': the perfect tense. Good news — you already own both halves of it.

blocks.annotated: {Olen|grammar|1st person, present of olla|I have} {käyttänyt|grammar|past participle|used} tätä huoltamoa monta vuotta.
blocks.translation: I have used this repair shop for many years.

blocks.title: Perfect tense as credibility
blocks.text: When a reviewer opens with olen käyttänyt or olen huollattanut, they're doing more than stating a fact — they're establishing standing before delivering a verdict. 'I've been using this place for five years' carries more weight than a first-time visit, and the perfect tense is exactly the grammatical shape that signals 'this isn't a one-off opinion'.
Piece 1 — Building the perfect: olla + past participle

blocks.content: The perfect tense is just two pieces you already have: the present tense of olla (Lesson 13: olen, olet, on...) plus the past participle (Lesson 3: -nut/-nyt). Käyttää (to use) → käyttänyt. Olen + käyttänyt → {olen käyttänyt|grammar|perfect tense|I have used}. No new endings to learn — just a new combination of two old ones.

items.fi: {Olen|grammar|1st person, present of olla|I have} {huollattanut|grammar|past participle|had serviced} autoni täällä viisi vuotta.
items.en: I have had my car serviced here for five years.

items.fi: {Olen|grammar|1st person, present of olla|I have} {saanut|grammar|past participle|gotten} aina hyvää palvelua.
items.en: I have always gotten good service.

blocks.text: Piece 2 — Third person perfect: on ollut, ovat löytyneet

blocks.content: The same combination works for 'he/she/it has' and 'they have' — just swap in the third-person forms of olla you already know: {on|grammar|3rd person, present of olla|has} for singular, {ovat|grammar|3rd person plural, present of olla|have} for plural. Hinta-arviot {ovat|grammar|3rd person plural, present of olla|have} hyvin {pitäneet|grammar|past participle, plural|held} paikkansa — 'the price estimates have held true well', reusing paikkansa from Lesson 14.

items.fi: Huolto {on|grammar|3rd person, present of olla|has} {ollut|grammar|past participle|been} aina asiallista.
items.en: The service has always been proper/professional.

items.fi: Viat {ovat|grammar|3rd person plural, present of olla|have} {löytyneet|grammar|past participle, plural|been found} nopeasti.
items.en: The faults have been found quickly.

blocks.text: Piece 3 — Negative perfect: en ole, ei ole

blocks.title: Same negation pattern as Lesson 3
blocks.text: Negating the perfect follows exactly the pattern from Lesson 3 — negation word + connegative — just with olla's connegative, ole, standing in for the main verb: {en ole|grammar|negative perfect, 1st person|I have not}, {ei ole|grammar|negative perfect, 3rd person|has not}. Työn jäljessä {ei ole|grammar|negative perfect, 3rd person|has not} ollut moittimista — 'there has been nothing to complain about in the work'.

items.fi: Työn jäljessä {ei ole|grammar|negative perfect, 3rd person|has not} ollut moittimista.
items.en: There has been nothing to complain about in the work.

items.fi: {En ole|grammar|negative perfect, 1st person|I have not} yrityksen palveluita aikaisemmin käyttänyt.
items.en: I have not used the company's services before.

lines.speaker: A
lines.fi: Kuinka kauan olet käyttänyt tätä korjaamoa?
lines.en: How long have you been using this repair shop?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Olen käyttänyt sitä monta vuotta, enkä ole koskaan pettynyt.
lines.en: I've used it for many years, and I have never been disappointed.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Have the price estimates held true?

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Yes, always. I strongly recommend it.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: The perfect tense will never surprise you again once you see it as addition, not invention: present-tense olla (Lesson 13) + past participle (Lesson 3). Every review you meet with olen/on/ovat sitting next to a -nut/-nyt word is building the same structure you can now build yourself.

blocks.content: Olen käyttänyt: O-len KÄYT-tä-nyt (two separate words, don't rush together — stress each on its own first syllable). Ovat löytyneet: O-vat LÖY-ty-neet (the 'öy' glides — round your lips for ö, then quickly to y).

blocks.title: What you now own
items: the perfect tense: olla (present) + past participle — built entirely from pieces you already had
olen käyttänyt, olen huollattanut — the loyal-customer opening line
on ollut, ovat löytyneet — third person perfect, singular and plural
en ole, ei ole — negative perfect, following Lesson 3's negation pattern exactly
you can now read the credibility-building opening of nearly every long-time-customer review in the corpus
